chunks: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmarri from al-Barqi from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Abi Khalaf from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The prayer of the two Eids with the Imam is a Sunnah, and there is no prayer before it or after it on that day until midday (az-zawal). If the Witr prayer is missed during your night, you pay it back after midday. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: We will clarify the meaning of this report later, God willing.

key_terms.إِلَى الزَّوَالِ: Until midday (when the sun begins to decline)
key_terms.صَلَاةُ الْعِيدَيْنِ: The two Eid prayers (Fitr and Adha)
key_terms.قَضَيْتَهُ: You pay it back / make it up

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing voluntary prayers before and after the Eid prayer, and how to make up the missed Witr?
ai.summary: This narration from the Tahdhib al-Ahkam, transmitted through the chain of Zurara, establishes the Eid prayers as a confirmed Sunnah when performed with the Imam, while explicitly prohibiting superfluous nafl prayers before or after until midday (az-zawal) to preserve the distinct sanctity of the day. It further clarifies the practical ruling for making up the Witr prayer, which is delayed until after the Eid prayer concludes, reflecting the Shia juristic view that Witr is not strictly bound to the night if missed. This ruling underscores the theological emphasis on following the Imam's lead during communal celebrations while maintaining specific temporal boundaries for individual devotions.
